motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is challenging; classical methods like the finite-temperature Lanczos method are limited by system size.
method: The quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM) uses a quantum computer to perform real-time evolution and compute thermal averages via a Lanczos-type approach.
result: The method is demonstrated on small systems and shows potential for near-term quantum devices, though no significant new physical insight is provided.
conclusion: QFTLM offers a hybrid quantum-classical approach for thermal state computations, but its practical advantage over classical methods remains to be proven.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic peaks at intermediate bond lengths, providing quantum information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes magic measures (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates.
result: Magic forms an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in binding energy, correlating with bond formation.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness offers new insight into molecular bonding, complementing entanglement measures.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation, a phase transition, could enable cells to process high-dimensional information, linking phase transitions to computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, and biomolecular condensates may provide a physical mechanism for information processing through phase transitions.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and perspective, drawing analogies between phase transitions and computational operations, without detailed mathematical modeling.
result: It proposes that condensates can act as sensors, classifiers, and responders to environmental cues, leveraging phase separation for information processing.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation offers a promising paradigm for cellular computation, but the ideas are speculative and require further experimental and theoretical validation.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to reduce the number of T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant T-count reduction compared to standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits by exploiting commuting structures.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
result: Demonstrates accurate learning of Floquet Hamiltonians and operator growth for several driven quantum models.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a scalable method for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, but the work is primarily a machine learning application without deep thermodynamic or information-theoretic insights.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify promising platforms for Majorana-based qubits, but the focus is on characterization rather than direct quantum information or thermodynamics applications.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel metastable phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory simulations.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photoinduced phase transitions, such as photodoping and transient order parameters, and discusses metastable superconducting and magnetic states.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions regarding thermalization and long-lived states.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from measurement conditions that break underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are widely used to constrain material properties, but some measurements exceed them, raising questions about validity and potential for novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a variety of fields and materials where such violations occur, analyzing which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that apparent violations are due to measurements made under conditions that do not satisfy the assumptions of the bounds, and that designed materials can exploit these violations.
conclusion: Understanding the assumptions behind thermodynamic bounds allows for the development of materials with properties that surpass classical limits, but this does not violate thermodynamics itself.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes to encode combinatorial Laplacians and achieve superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide quantum advantages for topological data analysis and related problems without relying on quantum oracles.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by using a state space of oriented simplices, enabling projection onto harmonic cycles. They also extend the framework to estimate persistent Betti numbers, verify QMA-hard problems, and solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem.
result: The quantum walk achieves apparent superpolynomial speedups over classical algorithms, provided the spectral gap is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes offer a promising approach for topological data analysis with significant speedups, though practical implementation depends on favorable spectral properties and sampling assumptions.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. Temporal coarse-graining is then achieved by conditioning the stochastic process on a coarse realization of the noise, expressing the conditioned stochastic process in terms of a sum of smooth, deterministic functions and bridge processes with boundaries fixed at zero, and performing the ensemble average over the bridge processes. For Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, the deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the stochastic bridge processes are not only independent but taken from the same distribution with correlators that can be expressed analytically, allowing the associated noise propagators to be precomputed once for all simulations. This combination of noise trajectories on a coarse time grid and ensemble averaging over bridge processes has practical advantages, such as a simple concatenation rule, that we highlight with numerical examples.

.
tldr: A method for simulating quantum systems with classical stochastic noise using temporal coarse-graining and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems with noise that has temporal correlations over many time scales (e.g., 1/f noise) is computationally challenging.
method: The noise is expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes; temporal coarse-graining conditions the process on a coarse realization, separating deterministic and bridge components, with the bridge ensemble averaged analytically.
result: The deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and bridge processes are independent with analytically known correlators, enabling precomputation of noise propagators.
conclusion: The approach offers practical advantages like a simple concatenation rule and is demonstrated with numerical examples.

title: Dynamics Of A Tracer Trapped In A Correlated Medium In The Presence Of A Wall
authors: Marcin Piotr Pruszczyk And Andrea Gambassi
abstract: We describe the random motion of a particle immersed in a thermally fluctuating medium and harmonically trapped at a certain distance from a wall. The medium, modeled by a Gaussian field with a tunable correlation length , is linearly coupled to the particle and evolves according to dissipative relaxational dynamics. Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on the field at the wall give rise to a repulsive fluctuation-induced force acting on the particle, causing a shift in its average position and a renormalization of the strength of the harmonic trap. We describe the effective overdamped dynamics of the particle, which features a nonlinear memory term depending on the wall-particle separation. We show that the two-time correlation function of the particle position features a memory-induced term that depends on the distance of the particle from the wall. At the critical point, this term decays algebraically upon increasing time and it displays a crossover from the behavior observed in the bulk to that corresponding to having the particle at the wall. Our results establish a concrete connection between boundary-induced modifications of critical fluctuations and the non-equilibrium, memory-dependent dynamics of a trapped particle.
tldr: The paper studies the dynamics of a tracer particle in a correlated medium near a wall, focusing on fluctuation-induced forces and memory effects.
motivation: To understand how boundaries modify critical fluctuations and affect the non-equilibrium dynamics of a trapped particle.
method: The medium is modeled as a Gaussian field with relaxational dynamics and Dirichlet boundary conditions; the particle's effective overdamped dynamics is derived analytically.
result: The two-time correlation function shows a memory-induced term that decays algebraically at the critical point, with a crossover from bulk to wall behavior.
conclusion: Boundary-induced modifications of critical fluctuations lead to memory-dependent dynamics, establishing a concrete connection between critical phenomena and non-equilibrium particle motion.

title: Symmetry-induced Logarithmic Relaxation In The Quantum Kicked Rotor
authors: Julien Hébraud, Floriane Arrouas, Bruno Peaudecerf, Juliette Billy, David Guéry-Odelin, Olivier Giraud, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié And Christian Miniatura
abstract: We study the effect of discrete symmetries on coherent multiple scattering in the quantum kicked rotor. When the initial momentum is set to zero—as in recent Bose–Einstein condensate experiments—the effective pseudo-disorder becomes even under momentum inversion. The resulting discrete mirror symmetry of the dynamics profoundly alters spectral correlations: it generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets localised at opposite momenta, whose exponentially small splittings produce a hierarchy of exponentially large dynamical timescales. The coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks then exhibit a striking non-monotonic evolution and strongly asymmetric contrasts, followed by an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation toward a common asymptotic value—a hallmark of glassy dynamics, here emerging in a fully coherent quantum system. That such archetypal glass-like behaviour arises from a single discrete symmetry constraint reveals an unexpected and deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation phenomena.
tldr: Discrete mirror symmetry in the quantum kicked rotor leads to quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets and logarithmic relaxation, revealing glassy dynamics in a coherent quantum system.
motivation: To understand how discrete symmetries affect coherent multiple scattering and spectral correlations in quantum systems, and to explore the emergence of slow relaxation phenomena.
method: Theoretical analysis of the quantum kicked rotor with a mirror symmetry constraint, using spectral statistics and dynamical simulations to study Floquet eigenstates and coherent backscattering.
result: Mirror symmetry generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets with exponentially small splittings, leading to non-monotonic evolution of coherent backscattering peaks and logarithmic relaxation to a common asymptotic value.
conclusion: A single discrete symmetry can produce glassy dynamics in a fully coherent quantum system, establishing a deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation.

title: Nonequilibrium Dimension-raising Phase Transitions
authors: Zhizhen Chen And Zi Cai
abstract: We propose a periodically driven system whose dimensionality is an emergent property that can be tunable, thus enables us to realize not only many-body phases with arbitrary dimensions, but also phase transitions, instead of crossovers, between phases with various dimensions. We study an interacting rotor model whose instantaneous Hamiltonian keeps the one-dimensional feature at any given time. Despite this, an emergent two-dimensional (2D) phase appears when the driving frequency exceeds a critical value, at which a dimension-raising phase transition takes place. We find that the nonequilibrium feature of the system could qualitatively change the finite temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase and make it different from its equilibrium counterpart. A four-dimensional generalization and experimental realizations of the proposed model based on a programmable reconfiguration technique in optical tweezers setups have also been discussed.
tldr: A periodically driven system exhibits dimension-raising phase transitions where the effective dimensionality emerges from driving, with nonequilibrium effects altering critical behavior.
motivation: To explore how periodic driving can induce phase transitions between phases of different effective dimensions, and to understand the nonequilibrium critical behavior of such emergent phases.
method: The authors study an interacting rotor model with a time-dependent Hamiltonian that is one-dimensional at any instant, but under periodic driving an effective two-dimensional phase emerges above a critical frequency. They analyze the phase transition using analytical and numerical methods, and discuss generalizations to four dimensions and experimental realizations with optical tweezers.
result: A dimension-raising phase transition occurs at a critical driving frequency, and the nonequilibrium nature qualitatively changes the finite-temperature critical behavior compared to equilibrium 2D systems.
conclusion: Periodic driving can be used to realize phases with tunable effective dimensions and phase transitions between them, offering a new platform for studying nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type memory effects in the orientational relaxation of nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by suppressing slow modes.
motivation: Understanding and overcoming memory effects that limit acceleration of relaxation in stochastic systems is important for controlling multiscale dynamics.
method: Optical birefringence measurements of field-induced orientation in polydisperse nanoparticle suspensions, combined with Smoluchowski equation modeling and multi-step field protocols.
result: Kovacs nonmonotonic relaxation is observed and attributed to polydispersity; sequential suppression of slow modes reduces relaxation time significantly.
conclusion: Memory effects in polydisperse systems can be mitigated by tailored multi-step protocols, providing a strategy for accelerating relaxation in soft matter.

title: Subgap Pumping Of Antiferromagnetic Mott Insulators: Photoexcitation Mechanisms And Applications
authors: Radu Andrei, Mingyao Guo, Mustafa G Ali, Hoon Kim, Richard D Averitt, David Hsieh And Eugene Demler
abstract: We study the behavior of the 2D repulsive Hubbard model on a square lattice at half filling, under strong driving with ac electric fields, by employing a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach. Within the same theoretical framework, we analytically obtain the conventional Keldysh crossover between multiphoton and tunneling photoexcitation mechanisms, as well as two new regimes beyond the Keldysh paradigm. We discuss how dynamical renormalization of the Mott–Hubbard gap feeds back into the photoexcitation process, modulating the carrier generation rate in real time. The momentum distribution of quasiparticle excitations immediately after the drive is calculated, and shown to contain valuable information about the generation mechanism. Finally, we discuss experimental probing of the pump-induced nonequilibrium electronic state.
tldr: The paper studies photoexcitation mechanisms in antiferromagnetic Mott insulators under strong ac driving, revealing regimes beyond the Keldysh crossover and dynamical gap renormalization.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems under intense light is crucial for controlling electronic phases and developing ultrafast optoelectronics.
method: A time-dependent Gaussian variational approach is applied to the 2D repulsive Hubbard model at half filling to simulate the response to ac electric fields.
result: Analytical derivation of conventional Keldysh crossover and two new photoexcitation regimes; dynamical renormalization of the Mott gap modulates carrier generation; momentum distribution of quasiparticles reveals generation mechanism.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for photoexcitation in Mott insulators and suggests experimental probes to access the non-equilibrium electronic state.

title: Quantum Entanglement, Stratified Spaces, And Topological Matter: Towards Entanglement-sensitive Langlands Data
authors: Kazuki Ikeda And Steven Rayan
abstract: Using the spinless Haldane model, we study the witness-filtered Berry curvature, quantum geometric tensor, and quantum Fisher information on the gapped strata of the parameter space and evaluate them through the Fukui–Hatsugai–Suzuki discretization. The filtered quantities isolate the part of the geometric response carried by sublattice coherence: they suppress contributions from regions where the occupied Bloch state is locally A/B-separable and emphasize regions where curvature and coherence coexist. We derive exact lattice identities, reconstruction formulas for the curvature-weighted coherence, and bounds relating the filtered quantum geometric tensor and quantum Fisher information to single-particle mode entanglement. Across the gap-closing stratum, the quantized response changes admit a natural description in terms of Hecke modifications. We elicit a corresponding Langlands viewpoint—not as a full correspondence, but as an organizational principle and as the mathematical shadow of these physical geometric constructions.
tldr: The paper uses the Haldane model to study filtered geometric quantities and connects them to entanglement and Langlands theory.
motivation: To isolate geometric response due to sublattice coherence and relate it to entanglement in topological matter.
method: Applies witness-filtered Berry curvature, quantum geometric tensor, and quantum Fisher information on gapped strata using Fukui–Hatsugai–Suzuki discretization.
result: Derives exact lattice identities, bounds linking filtered geometric tensors to single-particle mode entanglement, and describes quantized response changes via Hecke modifications.
conclusion: The Langlands viewpoint serves as an organizational principle for these physical geometric constructions.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
authors: Antonio Demarti Iolius
Imanol Etxezarreta Martinez
Joschka Roffe
Josu Etxezarreta Martinez
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: An almost-linear time decoding algorithm for quantum LDPC codes under circuit-level noise.
motivation: Efficient decoding of quantum LDPC codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing decoders are often too slow or assume simpler noise models.
method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm based on belief propagation with a novel scheduling and post-processing step that achieves almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm demonstrates high threshold and low logical error rates under circuit-level noise, with runtime scaling almost linearly with code length.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that is both fast and effective under realistic noise, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Ground State Preparation Of Random All-to-all Hamiltonians Using Adapt-vqe
authors: Sabhyata Gupta, Bharath Sambasivam, Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes, Alexander F. Kemper, Raghav G. Jha
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ground state of random Hamiltonians with all-to-all interactions such as the quantum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model follow volume-law entanglement and are expected to be hard to model using tensor networks. In recent years, some progress has been made to push the limit of classical methods using neural quantum states. However, it remains an open question whether there exist quantum algorithms that could offer a quantum advantage over the state-of-the-art classical methods in simulating random Hamiltonians. In this work, we show that one such algorithm, TETRIS-ADAPT-VQE, can construct accurate ground states for dense and sparse SYK models containing up to [MATH] Majorana fermions achieving fidelities [MATH] and for the quantum SK model with up to [MATH] sites achieving fidelities [MATH]. We find that while the preparation of ground states is efficient (in terms of operator pool size and circuit depth) for the SK model, it is not efficient for either dense or moderately sparse SYK models.
tldr: This paper uses a variational quantum algorithm (TETRIS-ADAPT-VQE) to prepare ground states of random all-to-all Hamiltonians (SYK and SK models), finding efficient preparation for SK but not for SYK.
motivation: Random all-to-all Hamiltonians like SYK and SK models are classically hard due to volume-law entanglement, and it is an open question whether quantum algorithms can offer advantage.
method: The authors apply the TETRIS-ADAPT-VQE algorithm, a variational quantum eigensolver with adaptive operator selection, to construct ground states of dense and sparse SYK models (up to 12 Majorana fermions) and the quantum SK model (up to 12 sites).
result: Ground states are prepared with high fidelity for SK models (efficient in operator pool size and circuit depth), but for SYK models the preparation is not efficient, requiring large operator pools and deep circuits.
conclusion: While ADAPT-VQE works well for SK models, it does not provide a quantum advantage for SYK models, suggesting that random all-to-all Hamiltonians with SYK-type interactions remain challenging for near-term quantum algorithms.

title: Gatekeepers And Hallucinations: A Layered Evaluation Framework For LLM-Driven Quantum Circuit Generation
authors: Sharon Marfatia Christopher Coleman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become embedded in quantum simulation workflows (IDE copilots, notebook assistants, agentic pipelines), evaluation must move beyond functional correctness to anticipate and catch structured failures before they propagate through expensive pipelines. We present a layered evaluation framework for materials-informed Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) circuit generation: (i) a gatekeeper screening rubric across seven physical and framework criteria; (ii) a circuit fidelity analysis comparing model outputs against analytical and reference-implementation values for H2/STO-3G/Jordan-Wigner/UCCSD, with ansatz classification and gate-composition breakdown; and (iii) design entropy, a run-to-run behavioral consistency metric. We surface a taxonomy of five distinct LLM failure modes (geometry hallucination, nonexistent API usage, runtime integration failures, constraint violations, and plausible-but-unverifiable output), each with distinct detectability profiles and structural to the task rather than to any one model. A forensic audit of the evaluation platform's own source code further establishes that two apparent model failures originated in the harness through silent fallback-template substitution, demonstrating that evaluation infrastructure belongs inside the same trust boundary as the models it tests. Applied across multiple foundation models on a Materials Project integrated pipeline, the framework shows that gatekeeper-style validation is necessary, not optional, for reliable deployment.
tldr: A framework for evaluating LLM-generated quantum circuits for VQE, focusing on failure modes and validation.
motivation: LLMs are increasingly used in quantum simulation workflows, but their outputs can contain structured failures that propagate through expensive pipelines.
method: The authors propose a layered evaluation framework including a gatekeeper rubric, circuit fidelity analysis, and a behavioral consistency metric called design entropy, applied to H2/STO-3G/Jordan-Wigner/UCCSD circuits.
result: They identify five distinct LLM failure modes and show that some apparent failures originated from the evaluation harness itself, not the models.
conclusion: Gatekeeper-style validation is necessary for reliable deployment of LLMs in quantum circuit generation.

title: Quantum Algorithm For Valiant-Vazirani Reduction
authors: Patrick Kelly, Victoria S. Ordonez, Michael R. Geller
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is growing interest in extensions of the standard model of gate-based quantum computation to include auxiliary degrees of freedom evolving according to a nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. By reducing the Boolean satisfiability problem SAT to quantum state discrimination, Abrams and Lloyd argued that the right type of nonlinearity can be used to solve {\sf NP} and \#{\sf P} problems in polynomial time, at least in an idealized noise-free limit. For practical implementation, however, we are restricted to simulated and emergent nonlinearities, such as that appearing in mean field models for ultracold atoms and similar ensembles. A prominent example is the torsion model, which arises in two-component Bose-Einstein condensates and spin models with all-to-all Ising interaction. But torsion-based state discrimination appears to fall short of solving SAT. Here we close this gap by constructing the filtered oracle of the Valiant-Vazirani theorem, providing a randomized polynomial-time reduction from SAT to UNIQUE SAT, a promise problem where there is at most 1 satisfying assignment. In the noise free limit, the UNIQUE SAT problem can be olved in polynomial time using torsion nonlinearity. Quantum Valiant-Vazirani reduction is no faster than the efficient classical version, but a fault-tolerant implementation coupled to a nonlinear quantum coprocessor simulating torsion would enable polynomial time solution to {\sf NP} (but not \#{\sf P}) problems.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm using nonlinear torsion to solve NP problems via Valiant-Vazirani reduction, but relies on non-standard nonlinear quantum mechanics.
motivation: To extend quantum computing beyond the standard linear model to solve NP-complete problems efficiently using nonlinear dynamics.
method: Constructs a filtered oracle for Valiant-Vazirani reduction to convert SAT to UNIQUE SAT, then uses torsion-based nonlinear state discrimination to solve UNIQUE SAT in polynomial time.
result: In the noise-free limit, the algorithm solves NP problems in polynomial time, but not #P problems; the reduction itself is no faster than classical.
conclusion: A fault-tolerant implementation with a nonlinear quantum coprocessor could enable polynomial-time solution to NP problems, but practical realization is challenging.

title: Measurement-enabled Online Quantum Processing With Amplitude Encoding
authors: Giacomo Franceschetto, Pere Mujal, Rodrigo Mart\'inez-Pe\~na
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a quantum reservoir computing online protocol that realizes amplitude encoding on quantum hardware. Our scheme combines mid-circuit measurement and reset operations to implement the partial-trace dynamics underlying amplitude encoding, while an indirect measurement scheme provides access to reservoir observables without interrupting temporal processing. In contrast to other approaches, our method preserves online operation, avoids input buffering, and keeps the runtime linear in the number of time steps. We present the theoretical formulation of the protocol and a proof-of-principle implementation on quantum hardware, and we evaluate its performance on two standard benchmark tasks. Our results show that the reservoir dynamics can be monitored through both direct measurements of the input qubits and indirect measurements of the memory qubits, enabling observation of the full system while isolating the internal evolution of the reservoir. This work provides a practical route toward scalable hardware implementations of amplitude-encoded quantum reservoir computing and opens the door to systematic experimental studies of complex quantum reservoirs.
tldr: A quantum reservoir computing protocol using amplitude encoding with mid-circuit measurements for online temporal processing.
motivation: To enable scalable online quantum reservoir computing without input buffering and with linear runtime.
method: Combines mid-circuit measurement and reset to implement partial-trace dynamics for amplitude encoding, and uses indirect measurements to access reservoir observables.
result: Demonstrates online operation on quantum hardware with linear runtime and shows that reservoir dynamics can be monitored via direct and indirect measurements.
conclusion: Provides a practical route to scalable hardware implementations of amplitude-encoded quantum reservoir computing.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality

abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the space-time duality approach and its relationship to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that preserve a symmetry subalgebra, which is a topic in quantum computation theory.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define two topological invariants: an anyon permutation map and a generalized GNVW index, and proves that these classify subalgebra QCAs up to finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs on one-dimensional spin systems with finite Abelian group symmetry, and demonstrates that the Kramers-Wannier duality corresponds to a nontrivial anyon permutation and has irrational index.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are strictly richer than full-algebra QCAs and cannot be extended to the full algebra, mixing nontrivially with translations.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement using spin-squeezed states in lossy multi-path atom interferometers, focusing on practical metrology.
motivation: Atom interferometry is limited by the standard quantum limit; spin-squeezed states can surpass it, but losses and finite temperature degrade performance.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses, and one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree yields several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic conditions, but finite temperature remains a significant challenge.

title: Hidden Time-nonlocal Floquet Symmetries
authors: Sigmund Kohler And Jesús Casado-Pascual
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2112 (2026).

We investigate the Floquet spectrum of a detuned, driven two-level system and show that it exhibits exact quasienergy crossings when the detuning is an integer multiple of the energy quantum of the driving field. This behavior can be explained by a hidden time-nonlocal parity, which allows the Floquet modes to be classified as even or odd. Then a generic feature is the emergence of exact crossings between quasienergies of different parity. A constructive proof of the existence of the symmetry is based on a scalar recurrence relation. Moreover, we present a general scheme for its numerical computation, which can be applied to models beyond the two-level system. Analytical results are illustrated with numerical data.

.
tldr: The paper studies hidden time-nonlocal Floquet symmetries in driven two-level systems, explaining exact quasienergy crossings via a parity classification.
motivation: Understanding exact quasienergy crossings in Floquet systems is important for controlling quantum dynamics, but the paper focuses on a specific symmetry property rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a scalar recurrence relation to construct a hidden time-nonlocal parity operator and numerically compute it for models beyond two-level systems.
result: Exact quasienergy crossings occur when detuning is an integer multiple of the driving quantum, and these crossings are protected by the hidden parity symmetry.
conclusion: The hidden symmetry provides a classification of Floquet modes and explains generic crossing features, but the work is primarily about Floquet theory and symmetry, not directly related to the user's research directions.

title: Constant Sensitivity Birefringence Metrology Using Vector Vortex Beams
authors: Gabriela Flores-Cova, Daniel Salamanca-Rold\'an, Carmelo Rosales-Guzm\'an, Daniel F. Urrego, Juan P. Torres
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) microscopy and chiral analysis are two imaging techniques that measure the birefringence, i.e., the phase difference introduced by a sample on two orthogonal polarizations. Conventional approaches employ Gaussian beams and infer birefringence from polarization changes, resulting in phase-estimation sensitivities that depend on the unknown phase. We demonstrate here a new type of birefringence detector. It makes use of a vector vortex beam, a type of structured light endowed with optical modes that carry opposite orbital angular momentum (OAM). Using quantum estimation theory tools, we demonstrate that the sensitivity of phase estimation is independent of the value of the unknown phase, and can be even better, in principle, than the conventional approach. We experimentally validate the proposed scheme, demonstrating the potential of structured light for robust and uniform birefringence sensing.
tldr: This paper uses vector vortex beams and quantum estimation theory to achieve constant-sensitivity birefringence metrology.
motivation: Conventional birefringence measurements have sensitivity that depends on the unknown phase; the authors aim to design a detector with uniform sensitivity.
method: They employ vector vortex beams carrying opposite orbital angular momentum and apply quantum estimation theory to analyze phase estimation sensitivity.
result: The sensitivity is independent of the unknown phase and can surpass conventional approaches; the scheme is validated experimentally.
conclusion: Structured light enables robust and uniform birefringence sensing, with potential applications in microscopy and chiral analysis.

title: Elastic Surface Instability As A Topological Phase Transition
authors: Yu-Xin Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The macroscopic instability of soft materials undergoing extreme deformations is traditionally viewed as a pure structural or mechanical failure. Driven by the quest to uncover universal principles across disparate physical systems, we bridge two vibrant yet seemingly disconnected research frontiers: macroscopic finite-strain solid mechanics and quantum-like topological physics. Here, we demonstrate that the classical elastic surface instability of a deformed hyperelastic manifold is not merely a mechanical bifurcation, but fundamentally a topological phase transition. By incorporating Lie group metric evolution into a generalized Stroh formalism, we map the highly nonlinear geometric frustration onto an algebraic surface impedance matrix [MATH]. For a semi-infinite hyperelastic half-space under finite compression, we analytically map the system to a one-dimensional Dirac Hamiltonian, where the macroscopic mechanical stretch acts as a tunable knob for the Dirac mass. We reveal that the onset of surface wrinkles marks a topological transition from a trivial to a non-trivial phase characterized by a quantized step in the winding number, naturally giving rise to a robust, macroscopically localized zero-energy edge state. This fundamental linkage unifies macroscopic symmetry breaking with the topological paradigm, opening a new theoretical pathway for programmable smart soft matter.
tldr: This paper maps elastic surface instability in soft materials to a topological phase transition using a Dirac Hamiltonian analogy.
motivation: To unify macroscopic solid mechanics with quantum topological physics, revealing that mechanical wrinkling is a topological transition.
method: Incorporates Lie group metric evolution into a generalized Stroh formalism and maps the system to a one-dimensional Dirac Hamiltonian.
result: The onset of surface wrinkles corresponds to a topological transition with a quantized winding number and a zero-energy edge state.
conclusion: Elastic instability is fundamentally a topological phase transition, opening avenues for programmable smart soft matter.

title: Self-averaging Of Replica Overlaps In The Random Field Edwards-Anderson Model
authors: Y. Sakamoto C. Itoi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The self-averaging of the replica overlap is proven in the Edwards-Anderson (EA) model under random field almost everywhere in the coupling constant space in any dimension. The EA order parameter is represented in terms of the derivative of the free energy density with respect to the random field strength, regardless of boundary conditions. Tasaki's correlation inequality for finite-dimensional spin glass models shows that the expectation of the squared replica overlap is bounded by the squared EA order parameter. These simple evaluations enable us to prove that the variance of the replica overlap vanishes in the infinite-volume limit. The self-averaging of the replica bond overlap is proven also in the EA model with Gaussian exchange interaction without random field. Short-range spin glass models have been shown to behave differently from mean-field spin glass models with RSB phase.
tldr: Proves self-averaging of replica overlaps in the random field Edwards-Anderson model using correlation inequalities.

title: Benchmark Of Pauli Correlation Encoding For Different Optimisation Problems
authors: Fernando Alonso, Colom\'an Sampr\'on, Jacobo Veiga, Mariamo Mussa Juane, Andr\'es G\'omez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The continuous progress of quantum technologies has spurred the exploration of their potential applications across diverse fields, particularly in combinatorial optimisation. In this work, we study a quantum-classical optimisation framework based on Pauli Correlation Encoding, an encoding scheme that can represent m binary variables using a polynomial number of qubits. To evaluate the performance of the method, we use four classical optimisation problems against the instances of the QOPTLib benchmark. The study includes an analysis of the impact of the compression order of the encoding scheme, the problem structure, and hyperparameter selection on solution quality, as well as the role of post-processing in improving performance. Additionally, we study the effect of shot-based execution and hardware noise, showing how these factors influence both the accuracy of expected value estimation and the overall dynamics of the optimisation process. The results indicate that the proposed PCE-based framework achieves competitive performance against the benchmark and, in several cases, obtains equivalent or even superior solutions, highlighting its potential as an efficient encoding strategy for quantum optimisation in the NISQ and near fault-tolerant era.
tldr: This paper benchmarks a quantum-classical optimization framework using Pauli Correlation Encoding for combinatorial problems, focusing on solution quality and noise effects.
motivation: To explore efficient encoding schemes for quantum optimization in the NISQ era, reducing qubit count while maintaining performance.
method: The authors apply Pauli Correlation Encoding to map binary variables to a polynomial number of qubits, test on four classical optimization problems from QOPTLib, and analyze compression order, hyperparameters, post-processing, shot noise, and hardware noise.
result: The PCE-based framework achieves competitive or superior solutions compared to the benchmark, with performance influenced by encoding order and noise.
conclusion: Pauli Correlation Encoding is a promising strategy for quantum optimization, but practical deployment requires careful handling of noise and hyperparameters.

title: Thermodynamic-Kinetic Decoupling Enables Stable Excitonic Emission In Defect-Tolerant Cu-Based Quantum Dots
authors: Haoran Chen, Zhipeng Xu, Chunjian Li, Lei Hou, Dechao Yu, Xiaobin Xie, Yue Liu, Bohua Dong, Lixin Cao, Chenghui Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Colloidal quantum dots that simultaneously offer room-temperature single-photon purity and high photoluminescence quantum yield are sought for quantum optics, but remain elusive in environmentally benign materials. We introduce a thermodynamic-kinetic decoupling strategy that transforms defect-tolerant CuInS2 quantum dots into bright, narrowband, and photostable single-photon emitters. Zn2+ alloying strains the lattice, thermodynamically suppressing native copper vacancies and narrowing the emission from a broad defect band of approximately 300 meV to an excitonic line of approximately 120 meV. Ga3+ incorporation then kinetically pins the cation sublattice against Cu+ migration, preventing defect regeneration during ZnS shell growth. The resulting Cd-free core/shell dots achieve near-unity quantum yield of approximately 98% while retaining narrow excitonic emission. Critically, room-temperature single-dot spectroscopy reveals homogeneous linewidths as low as approximately 58 meV, strongly suppressed blinking, and high-purity single-photon emission with g2(0) = 0.06. This stabilized excitonic emission directly reduces reabsorption losses in luminescent solar concentrators, yielding an external optical efficiency of 12.68%. Our work establishes a generalizable framework to unlock intrinsic excitonic photophysics in ion-mobile, defect-prone semiconductors, opening a viable path toward high-performance heavy-metal-free emitters for quantum light sources.
tldr: This paper presents a thermodynamic-kinetic decoupling strategy to stabilize excitonic emission in CuInS2 quantum dots, achieving near-unity quantum yield and single-photon purity.
motivation: Colloidal quantum dots that combine room-temperature single-photon purity and high photoluminescence quantum yield are needed for quantum optics, but are lacking in environmentally benign materials.
method: Zn2+ alloying strains the lattice to suppress native copper vacancies, and Ga3+ incorporation kinetically pins the cation sublattice against Cu+ migration during ZnS shell growth.
result: The Cd-free core/shell dots achieve ~98% quantum yield, narrow excitonic emission (~120 meV), homogeneous linewidths as low as ~58 meV, suppressed blinking, and single-photon emission with g2(0)=0.06.
conclusion: This work provides a generalizable framework to unlock intrinsic excitonic photophysics in defect-prone semiconductors, enabling heavy-metal-free quantum light sources.

title: Not Your Usual Fft: QFT$\rightarrow$FFT Via Classical Quantum-Circuit Simulation
authors: Stefano Markidis, Gilbert Netzer, Luca Pennati, Frej Larssen, Ivy Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce QFT[MATH]FFT, a family of HPC FFT libraries that compute the discrete Fourier transform by executing a quantum Fourier transform (QFT) circuit on classical quantum computer simulators. Input arrays are mapped directly to state amplitudes with explicit normalization/indexing, making QFT a drop-in replacement for FFT primitives. A backend-agnostic planner builds a fused-gate schedule and memory layout adapters to increase arithmetic intensity and reduce memory data movement. We implement this design on top of Google's C++ and evaluate OpenMP, AVX, and CUDA backends. On an AMD EPYC Zen2 processor, our AVX performance is on par with that of multithreaded FFTW, utilizing 64 threads. On an NVIDIA A100, the CUDA backend achieves more than [MATH] lower time than both AVX and FFTW on AMD EPYC Zen2 at larger sizes. We also employ an approximate QFT (AQFT) that truncates small-angle controlled rotations beyond a cutoff [MATH], reducing circuit depth and runtime while preserving accuracy.
tldr: This paper presents a method to compute classical FFTs by simulating quantum Fourier transform circuits on classical hardware, achieving competitive performance.
motivation: To leverage quantum circuit simulation for classical computation, potentially offering new algorithmic approaches or performance benefits.
method: The authors map input arrays to quantum state amplitudes, construct a fused-gate schedule, and implement backends using OpenMP, AVX, and CUDA on classical simulators.
result: The AVX backend matches multithreaded FFTW on AMD EPYC, and the CUDA backend outperforms both on NVIDIA A100. Approximate QFT reduces circuit depth with minimal accuracy loss.
conclusion: Classical simulation of QFT can serve as a practical FFT library, but the work is primarily a classical HPC optimization with no quantum information or thermodynamics contribution.

authors: Ryosuke Kurihara, Atsuhiko Miyata, Koji Araki, Shusaku Imajo, Ruo Hibino, Atsushi Miyake, Sergei Zherlitsyn, Joachim Wosnitza, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Fumitoshi Iga, Masashi Tokunaga, And Yasuhiro H. Matsuda
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Kurihara, Atsuhiko Miyata, Koji Araki, Shusaku Imajo, Ruo Hibino, Atsushi Miyake, Sergei Zherlitsyn, Joachim Wosnitza, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Fumitoshi Iga, Masashi Tokunaga, and Yasuhiro H. Matsuda

Quantum oscillations in the Kondo insulator YbB
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235129] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasonic measurements in YbB12 find no magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations in the insulating phase, contrasting with transport and magnetocaloric signals.
motivation: Quantum oscillations in insulators challenge conventional Fermi surface theory; the authors aim to resolve inconsistencies by probing elastic constants.
method: High-field ultrasonic measurements of elastic constants in YbB12 single crystals, compared with transport and magnetocaloric oscillations.
result: No magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations detected in the elastic constant, despite clear oscillations in transport and magnetocaloric data.
conclusion: The absence of elastic anomalies suggests that the quantum oscillations in insulators may not arise from conventional Landau quantization, pointing to an exotic electronic state.

title: Effect Of Spin-orbit Coupling On Spin And Orbital Ordering In ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{n+1}{\mathrm{Cr}}_{n}{\mathrm{O}}_{3n+1}$ ($n=1$, 2)
authors: Cristian Fanjul And A. A. Aligia
abstract:
Author(s): Cristian Fanjul and A. A. Aligia

We incorporate spin-orbit coupling (SOC) into effective Kugel-Khomskii models for the [MATH] and [MATH] members of the Ruddlesden-Popper series [MATH]. These models contain interacting spins 1 and pseudospins 1/2 at each site describing spin and orbit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235130] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-orbit coupling effects on spin and orbital ordering in Sr-based Ruddlesden-Popper compounds using effective Kugel-Khomskii models.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling with spin and orbital degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems.
method: Effective Kugel-Khomskii models are derived and analyzed, incorporating spin-orbit coupling for the n=1 and n=2 members of the Ruddlesden-Popper series.
result: The models predict specific spin and orbital ordering patterns influenced by spin-orbit coupling.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling significantly modifies the ordering, which can be tested experimentally.

title: Paramagnetic Instability In A Tubular Nanowire With Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions
authors: R. A. Perrin And D. C. Marinescu
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Perrin and D. C. Marinescu

We describe a case of instability of the paramagnetic order in an electron gas confined in a thin tubular semiconductor nanowire with a Rashba spin-orbit interaction. This situation is realized when, for a critical value of the Rashba coupling constant [MATH], dependent only on the radius of the …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235310] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies paramagnetic instability in a tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, a condensed matter physics topic without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the magnetic phase transition in a confined electron gas with spin-orbit interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of an electron gas confined in a thin tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit interaction, solving for critical coupling constants.
result: A critical value of the Rashba coupling constant is found, dependent only on the nanowire radius, at which paramagnetic order becomes unstable.
conclusion: The work describes a specific instability mechanism in a nanowire system, relevant to spintronics but not to the user's research directions.

title: Persistent Current And Orbital Magnetization Along A Valley-contrasting Junction In Bilayer Graphene In A Magnetic Field
authors: K. Shizuya
abstract:
Author(s): K. Shizuya

In a magnetic field, bilayer graphene hosts an octet of pseudo-zero-mode (PZM) electron levels nearly degenerate in orbitals [MATH], valleys, and spins. They split in valleys by electrostatic gating. In gated bilayer graphene, in which the interlayer bias is set up to flip sign across a line, one…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235422] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies persistent current and orbital magnetization in a valley-contrasting junction in bilayer graphene under a magnetic field.
motivation: To understand the electronic properties of gated bilayer graphene with a sign-changing interlayer bias, which creates a valley-contrasting junction.
method: Theoretical analysis using a low-energy continuum model for bilayer graphene in a magnetic field, solving for pseudo-zero-mode levels and computing persistent current and orbital magnetization.
result: The valley-contrasting junction leads to valley-polarized persistent currents and orbital magnetization that depend on the junction geometry and magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings reveal new magneto-electronic phenomena in bilayer graphene junctions relevant for valleytronics.

title: Signatures Of Thermally Driven Evolution Of Fermi Surface Topology In Resistance Fluctuation Spectroscopy Of ${\mathrm{T}}_{d}\text{−}{\mathrm{WTe}}_{2}$
authors: Prajna Paromita Chanda, Subhajit Mondal, Najrul Islam, Vineet Pandey, Prasenjit Ghosh, Abhijith M B, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Saquib Shamim, And Vidya Kochat
abstract:
Author(s): Prajna Paromita Chanda, Subhajit Mondal, Najrul Islam, Vineet Pandey, Prasenjit Ghosh, Abhijith M B, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Saquib Shamim, and Vidya Kochat

Three-dimensional topological semimetals like type-II Weyl semimetal transition metal dichalcogenides [MATH] exhibit intriguing phenomena associated with various symmetries governing their band structure. Density functional theory-based band struc…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies resistance fluctuations in WTe2 to probe thermally driven changes in Fermi surface topology, a condensed matter physics topic unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how temperature-induced changes in Fermi surface topology affect electronic transport in type-II Weyl semimetal WTe2.
method: Combines density functional theory band structure calculations with resistance fluctuation spectroscopy measurements on exfoliated WTe2 flakes.
result: Identifies signatures of Lifshitz transitions in the noise spectrum, correlating with changes in the Fermi surface topology.
conclusion: Resistance fluctuation spectroscopy is a sensitive tool to detect topological changes in the Fermi surface of Weyl semimetals.

title: Magnetoelectric Subbands In The One-dimensional To Quasi-one-dimensional Confined Regime
authors: Yingshi Duo, Joshua Coop, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, And Sanjeev Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Yingshi Duo, Joshua Coop, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, and Sanjeev Kumar

We investigate the evolution of conductance quantization and subband structure in a weakly confined quasi-one-dimensional channel as a function of carrier density and perpendicular magnetic field. As the carrier density is reduced, the [MATH] plateau is progressively suppressed and an avoided …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetoelectric subbands and conductance quantization in a quasi-one-dimensional channel under magnetic field, focusing on carrier density effects.
motivation: To understand the evolution of subband structure and conductance plateaus in weakly confined quantum wires as carrier density and magnetic field vary.
method: Experimental transport measurements on a quasi-one-dimensional channel, analyzing conductance quantization and subband features as a function of carrier density and perpendicular magnetic field.
result: Observation of progressive suppression of the 2e²/h plateau and avoided crossings in subband dispersion, indicating magnetoelectric subband formation.
conclusion: The results reveal complex subband structure in the 1D to quasi-1D transition regime, relevant for understanding quantum transport in low-dimensional systems.

title: Exciton-induced Frequency Shift In High-harmonic Generation From Solids
authors: Xiang Li, Tong Wu, Jianshi Lu, Zitan Zuo, Shengzhe Pan, Shicheng Jiang, And Jian Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Tong Wu, Jianshi Lu, Zitan Zuo, Shengzhe Pan, Shicheng Jiang, and Jian Wu

Spectroscopy serves as a key experimental pathway for probing many-body dynamics. Among them, high-harmonic generation (HHG) spectroscopy is particularly valued for its subcycle temporal resolution. Recent investigations have confirmed that excitonic effects in crystals can significantly enhance har…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214315] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exciton-induced frequency shifts in high-harmonic generation from solids, focusing on many-body effects in HHG spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand how excitonic effects modify high-harmonic generation in solids, which is important for probing many-body dynamics with subcycle temporal resolution.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the influence of excitons on HHG spectra, likely using a semiconductor Bloch equation or similar framework to model electron-hole interactions.
result: Excitonic effects cause a frequency shift in the high-harmonic spectrum, which can be used to extract information about exciton binding energies and dynamics.
conclusion: Exciton-induced frequency shifts provide a new spectroscopic tool for studying many-body effects in solids via HHG.

title: Josephson Effects In The Spin-triplet Superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet Superconductor Junctions: The Detection Of The Intrinsic $d$-vector
authors: Ya-Ting Han, Li-Juan Chen, Wen-Ting Liu, Qiang Cheng, And Qing-Feng Sun
