motivation: Termination analysis of lasso programs is a challenging problem in program verification, and existing tools lack a unified, modular framework.
method: PaSTTeL is a modular, generic parallel portfolio framework that integrates multiple termination analysis algorithms, executes them concurrently, and can be embedded as a library.
result: Initial experiments show competitive performance against state-of-the-art termination analysis tools.
conclusion: PaSTTeL provides a flexible and efficient platform for termination and non-termination analysis, but is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Trap: Benchmark For Task-completion And Resistance To Active Privacy-extraction
authors: Moon Ye-Bin, Nam Hyeon-Woo, Baek Seong-Eun, Yejin Yeo, Tae-Hyun Oh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents are increasingly deployed in document-intensive workflows where sensitive private information is not an edge case but a routine input, e.g., an agent booking a flight needs passport numbers. In such settings, the agent must use private information to complete tasks accurately while never exposing it in its responses, because it cannot verify who is actually at the keyboard. These two obligations are in fundamental tension. A model capable enough to use private information for task completion can, by the same capability, be induced to reveal it. To evaluate the trade-off of task accuracy and privacy leakage, we introduce Task-completion and Resistance to Active Privacy-extraction (TRAP). Each scenario includes a document containing private information, a task query that requires the agent to invoke the correct tool using private fields, and an attack query that attempts to elicit the same information in natural language. Evaluating 22 models spanning frontier proprietary and open-source models at multiple scales, we find that all model families exhibit non-trivial leakage, and that instruction-following ability correlates with leakage rate. Existing prompt-based defenses reduce leakage but at significant cost to task accuracy. Prompt optimization fails to escape this trade-off. We demonstrate that this failure is not incidental. For any softmax-based model, no soft-constraint defense, e.g., prompt-based defenses, can jointly achieve high task success with zero leakage probability. Motivated by this impossibility result, we propose structural private field isolation, which replaces private fields with hash keys before they reach the model. This approach largely prevents leakage while keeping task accuracy.
tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating the trade-off between task completion and privacy leakage in AI agents handling private documents, and proposes a structural defense.
motivation: AI agents increasingly handle sensitive private information in document workflows, creating a tension between using that information for tasks and preventing its leakage.
method: The authors design the TRAP benchmark with task and attack queries, evaluate 22 models, and prove an impossibility result for soft-constraint defenses, then propose structural private field isolation using hash keys.
result: All models exhibit non-trivial leakage; instruction-following correlates with leakage; prompt-based defenses reduce leakage but hurt task accuracy; structural isolation prevents leakage while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: Soft-constraint defenses cannot jointly achieve high task success and zero leakage, but structural isolation offers a practical solution.

title: Lifecycle-Aware Dynamic Analysis For Secure Ml Model Execution
authors: Gabriele Digregorio, Marco Di Gennaro, Francesco Pastore, Stefano Zanero, Stefano Longari, Michele Carminati
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing reliance on pre-trained Machine Learning (ML) models has introduced new attack surfaces. Recent vulnerabilities demonstrate that malicious behavior can be embedded within model artifacts, often bypassing existing defenses. Current model-scanning solutions primarily rely on static, format-specific rules or known attack signatures, which limit their ability to generalize across frameworks and to detect novel exploitation paths. In contrast, we propose a solution that focuses on the effects an attack has on the host system executing the model and builds on foundational intuitions about ML model execution. In particular, we observe that ML models operate within well-defined lifecycle phases and that, within each phase, interactions with the host system are highly structured and predictable. We translate these intuitions into Moat, a dynamic lifecycle-aware approach for securing ML model execution, and instantiate this design in Re-Moat, our reference implementation. We evaluate Re-Moat across multiple ML frameworks using 77,974 real-world model artifacts from the Hugging Face Hub, 31 Proofs-of-Concept (PoCs) from CVEs, and 334 models from a state-of-the-art dataset, and compare it against state-of-the-art model-scanning solutions. Our results show that our approach detects all evaluated attack classes while maintaining a close-to-zero false-positive rate, validating our intuitions and motivating dynamic analysis for securing ML model execution.
tldr: This paper presents a dynamic analysis approach for detecting malicious behavior in ML model artifacts by monitoring host system interactions during model execution.
motivation: Existing static model-scanning solutions fail to generalize across frameworks and detect novel attacks, motivating a dynamic approach that observes runtime behavior.
method: The authors propose Moat, a lifecycle-aware dynamic analysis framework that monitors system calls and interactions during ML model execution phases, implemented as Re-Moat.
result: Evaluation on 77,974 real-world models and 31 CVEs shows detection of all attack classes with near-zero false positives, outperforming state-of-the-art static scanners.
conclusion: Dynamic lifecycle-aware analysis is effective for securing ML model execution and can complement existing static defenses.

title: Pypiline: Malicious PyPI Package Detection Via Suspicious Api Knowledge And Agent Workflow
authors: Siyuan Pang, Zhengwei Jiang, Yepeng Yao, Zijing Fan, Haozhe Li, Baoxu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection of malicious PyPI packages is crucial for maintaining the security of the open source software supply chain. Existing methods, which primarily rely on rules or traditional machine learning, suffer from poor interpretability and difficulty in adapting to novel attacks. To address this, we propose PYPILINE, a novel detection method that combines a suspicious API knowledge base with an Agent workflow. PYPILINE first conducts static analysis on known malicious packages, extracting abstract syntax trees and generating API call graphs, from which it automatically extracts and constructs a structured suspicious API knowledge base. During the detection phase, this knowledge base is used to enhance reasoning capabilities. Through an Agent workflow, PYPILINE performs in depth semantic analysis of unknown packages and outputs a structured, interpretable maliciousness assessment report. The experimental results show that PYPILINE significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art tools in precision of 96.7\%, recall of 99.6\%, and F1-score of 98.1\%, with its precision surpassing baseline tools by 5.7 to 24.2 percentage points. Additionally, we conducted an empirical study on malicious packages, systematically revealing prevalent attack strategies, as well as the most commonly abused APIs. Equipped with tool-calling AI agent workflows for automated vector database retrieval of suspicious API knowledge and mail server delivery of analysis reports, PYPILINE delivers a practical, efficient, and convenient malicious package detection solution to strengthen open-source ecosystem security.
tldr: This paper presents a method for detecting malicious PyPI packages using a suspicious API knowledge base and an AI agent workflow.
motivation: Existing malicious package detection methods suffer from poor interpretability and difficulty adapting to novel attacks.
method: PYPILINE performs static analysis on known malicious packages to build a structured suspicious API knowledge base, then uses an Agent workflow for semantic analysis of unknown packages.
result: The method achieves 96.7% precision, 99.6% recall, and 98.1% F1-score, outperforming state-of-the-art tools by 5.7 to 24.2 percentage points in precision.
conclusion: PYPILINE provides a practical, efficient, and interpretable solution for malicious package detection in the open-source ecosystem.

title: Compute-Budgeted Exploitability Evidence Graphs For Prospective Vulnerability Triage
authors: Taylan Alpay Faruk Alpay
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Defenders cannot patch every newly disclosed vulnerability at once, so exploitability prediction must be evaluated prospectively rather than retrospectively. We study compute-budgeted vulnerability triage in which each CVE is scored only from public evidence visible by a fixed decision time. Advisories, exploit archives, fix commits, and hacker-community discourse are represented as a temporal evidence graph; a budgeted selector admits only a few evidence documents per CVE, and every score is paired with an auditable certificate listing the supporting signals, timestamps, source layers, and leakage flags. On 12012 prospective CVEs from public sources, budgeted evidence selection raises leakage-safe prospective recall@50 from 0.010 for a severity-only baseline to 0.026, while two evidence documents per CVE capture most of the value. A strong cross-encoder reranker lowers prospective recall to 0.016, showing that semantic relevance to a CVE is not the same as evidence of exploitation. Most importantly, a naive random split with unfiltered evidence inflates apparent prospective recall by 8.5x and EPSS-high recall by 5.0x. The main contribution is a leakage-safe evaluation protocol and reproducible evidence certificates for contestable vulnerability-prioritization claims.
tldr: This paper proposes a compute-budgeted vulnerability triage method using temporal evidence graphs for prospective exploitability prediction.
motivation: Defenders cannot patch all vulnerabilities immediately, so they need to prioritize based on exploitability predictions that are evaluated prospectively to avoid data leakage.
method: The authors construct temporal evidence graphs from advisories, exploit archives, fix commits, and hacker discourse, then apply a budgeted selector to admit only a few evidence documents per CVE, and pair each score with an auditable certificate.
result: On 12,012 prospective CVEs, budgeted evidence selection improves leakage-safe prospective recall@50 from 0.010 to 0.026, and two evidence documents per CVE capture most of the value. A naive random split inflates recall by 8.5x.
conclusion: The main contribution is a leakage-safe evaluation protocol and reproducible evidence certificates for contestable vulnerability-prioritization claims.

title: Quantifying Compromise Risk In Exceptional Access Architectures Under Sparse And Indirect Evidence
authors: Alan Woodward
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lawful exceptional access (EA) systems hold the cryptographic keys that decrypt protected communications for authorised parties. The debate over their risks has been long and qualitative, complicated by two problems: no public dataset of EA-specific compromise events exists, so assessment must use sparse, indirect evidence; and prior work has treated structurally different designs as equivalent, though transmission-layer EA in carrier infrastructure (T-EA) and over-the-top EA at the platform layer (OTT-EA) differ in how cryptographic keys relate to ciphertext data. This paper builds a structured uncertainty framework for evaluating systemic compromise risk in EA architectures. It does not produce predictive forecasts, which the evidence cannot support; it separates findings robust to assumptions from those that depend on calibration. Four analytical layers are applied to T-EA and OTT-EA: three empirical pillars (historical analogues, a Monte Carlo scenario layer, a channel-independence decomposition) plus a Bayesian Structural Risk Model on a parallel-subgraph attack graph. The central findings are structural. First, EA-equipped architectures of either class carry strictly higher modelled risk than their no-EA counterfactual, an ordering independent of calibration. Second, the classes differ in distribution shape: T-EA risk is dominated by central tendency, OTT-EA by the tail under correlated campaigns. Third, calibration-conditional annual probability ranges span 1.4% to 12.9% for T-EA across the structured-judgement targeting-premium interval. Over multi-decade horizons, cumulative compromise is well above zero; key-material exfiltration is irreversible, weighing heavily on OTT-EA's larger user populations. The framework quantifies compromise probability, not expected harm; consequence modelling and benefit estimation are outside its scope.
tldr: This paper develops a structured uncertainty framework for evaluating systemic compromise risk in lawful exceptional access architectures using sparse and indirect evidence.
motivation: The debate over risks of exceptional access systems has been qualitative and hampered by lack of data and conflation of different designs.
method: The paper applies four analytical layers: historical analogues, Monte Carlo scenario layer, channel-independence decomposition, and a Bayesian Structural Risk Model on a parallel-subgraph attack graph.
result: EA-equipped architectures carry strictly higher modelled risk than no-EA counterfactual; T-EA risk is dominated by central tendency while OTT-EA risk is tail-dominated; annual compromise probability ranges from 1.4% to 12.9%.
conclusion: The framework quantifies compromise probability but not expected harm; cumulative compromise over multi-decade horizons is well above zero, with key-material exfiltration being irreversible.

title: Giskard : Byzantine Robust And Confidential Aggregation For Large-Scale Decentralized Learning
authors: Ousmane Touat, C\'esar Sabater, Mohamed Maouche, Sonia Ben Mokhtar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dealing simultaneously with confidentiality and Byzantine behaviors in decentralized learning is a challenging problem. Indeed, in decentralized learning, clients train a machine learning model while keeping their data locally and share their model parameters or gradients with a set of neighbors. While enforcing confidentiality calls for hiding the exchanged model parameters/gradients (e.g., by using cryptographic techniques), dealing with Byzantine contributions often requires inspecting the latter. Hence, most research works address these objectives separately. A recent line of work proposes to employ secure multi-party computation (MPC) to implement robust aggregators against model poisoning, thereby enforcing both confidentiality and Byzantine resilience. However, these solutions scale badly: they either require all-to-all communication between participants or delegate the entire computation to a small subset, whose computational and communication load grows proportionally with the size of the network. In this paper, we present Giskard, a protocol for confidential and Byzantine-robust decentralized aggregation. Giskard organizes [MATH] parties into a tree of committees of size [MATH] and evaluates a coordinate-wise approximate median via a committee-adapted distributed binary search over the value domain, using BGW-style MPC within each committee. We assess Giskard both theoretically by proving its security and confidentiality properties and experimentally through extensive experiments involving up to one million participants. Compared to its closest competitors, Giskard reduces per-party communication complexity asymptotically while exhibiting comparable model utility under up to [MATH] Byzantine parties.
tldr: Giskard is a protocol for Byzantine-robust and confidential aggregation in decentralized learning using secure multi-party computation.
motivation: Existing solutions for decentralized learning either sacrifice confidentiality for Byzantine resilience or scale poorly due to all-to-all communication or heavy delegation.
method: Giskard organizes parties into a tree of committees and computes a coordinate-wise approximate median via committee-adapted distributed binary search using BGW-style MPC within each committee.
result: The protocol reduces per-party communication complexity asymptotically compared to competitors and maintains model utility under up to 45% Byzantine parties, demonstrated with up to one million participants.
conclusion: Giskard achieves both confidentiality and Byzantine robustness in a scalable manner for large-scale decentralized learning.

title: OpenAnt: LLM-Powered Vulnerability Discovery Through Code Decomposition, Adversarial Verification, And Dynamic Testing
authors: Gadi Evron Nahum Korda
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated vulnerability discovery in large codebases remains challenging: traditional static analysis produces high false-positive rates, while dynamic approaches such as fuzzing require substantial infrastructure and often target narrow classes of bugs. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) enable semantic reasoning about program behavior, but applying LLMs to repository-scale security analysis introduces challenges related to context management, cost, and verification. We present OpenAnt, an open-source vulnerability discovery system that integrates static program analysis with LLM-based reasoning in a multi-stage pipeline. OpenAnt introduces three key techniques. First, codebases are decomposed into self-contained analysis units filtered by reachability from external entry points, reducing the analysis surface by up to 97% while preserving attack-relevant code. Second, candidate vulnerabilities undergo adversarial verification through constrained attacker simulation, where the model evaluates exploitability under realistic attacker capabilities. Third, findings are validated through dynamic verification, in which exploit environments are generated automatically, executed in sandboxed containers, and discarded after use. Evaluation on widely used open-source projects including OpenSSL, WordPress, and Flowise shows that this architecture can identify previously unknown vulnerabilities while maintaining manageable analysis cost and substantially reducing false positives. Our results suggest that closed-loop vulnerability discovery pipelines, combining semantic reasoning with exploit validation, provide a practical path toward scalable automated security analysis. OpenAnt is released as open source under the Apache 2.0 license at [URL].
tldr: OpenAnt uses LLMs and static/dynamic analysis to discover vulnerabilities in large codebases.
motivation: Automated vulnerability discovery suffers from high false positives and infrastructure overhead; LLMs offer semantic reasoning but face context and cost challenges.
method: The system decomposes code into reachable units, performs adversarial verification via constrained attacker simulation, and validates findings through dynamic testing in sandboxed containers.
result: Evaluation on OpenSSL, WordPress, and Flowise identified previously unknown vulnerabilities with reduced false positives and manageable cost.
conclusion: Closed-loop pipelines combining semantic reasoning with exploit validation enable scalable automated security analysis.

title: PhantomSkill: Malicious Code Injection In Agent Skill Ecosystems
authors: Chia-Mu Yu Yu-Ting Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills allow LLM-based coding agents to acquire domain-specific capabilities from third-party packages, but they also introduce a new supply-chain attack surface. We present PhantomSkill, an attack framework that hides malicious behavior in a skill's auxiliary resources rather than in its textual description. Its core technique, VulMask, rewrites overt malicious scripts into vulnerability-shaped implementations whose malicious behavior is activated only under attacker-controlled trigger conditions. This design shifts the visible signal from explicit malicious intent to ordinary-looking insecure code. Across representative host skills, attack goals, coding agents, generation models, and automated reviewers, VulMask preserves benign utility while reducing warning and malware-level detection compared with overt malicious scripts. Our results show that skill ecosystems require resource-level vetting, execution-time containment, and security policies that treat exploitable vulnerabilities in agent skills as potential malicious payloads.
tldr: This paper presents an attack framework for injecting malicious code into LLM-based coding agent skill ecosystems via auxiliary resources.
motivation: Agent skills introduce a new supply-chain attack surface; existing vetting focuses on textual descriptions, leaving auxiliary resources unchecked.
method: The VulMask technique rewrites malicious scripts into vulnerability-shaped implementations that activate only under attacker-controlled triggers, making them appear as ordinary insecure code.
result: The attack preserves benign utility while reducing detection rates compared to overt malicious scripts across various agents and reviewers.
conclusion: Skill ecosystems require resource-level vetting and execution-time containment to defend against such attacks.

title: The More The Merrier: Combining Properties For ABox Abduction Under Repair Semantics For ELbot
authors: Anselm Haak, Patrick Koopmann, Yasir Mahmood, Anni-Yasmin Turhan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abduction is a central approach to explain missing entailments from a knowledge base by providing a hypothesis, that would, if added to the knowledge base, make the missing entailment become true. Abduction under repair semantics has recently been investigated in detail, where several desirable properties and optimality criteria were considered, such as signature-restrictions and minimality in size and of introduced conflicts. Naturally, hypotheses that satisfy more than one of these properties or combine a property with an optimality criterion would be even more desirable for applications. So far, such hypotheses have not been investigated in the literature. In the present paper, we consider the ABox abduction problem for hypotheses satisfying more than one property or additional optimality criteria, for EL_bot under brave and AR semantics. Our main observation is that often requiring additional properties for hypotheses does not lead to an increase of complexity.
tldr: This paper studies ABox abduction under repair semantics for the description logic EL_bot, focusing on combining multiple properties and optimality criteria.
motivation: To generate explanations for missing entailments in knowledge bases, hypotheses satisfying multiple desirable properties are needed, but such combinations have not been studied before.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of ABox abduction for EL_bot under brave and AR semantics when requiring multiple properties (e.g., signature restrictions, minimality) simultaneously.
result: Requiring additional properties for hypotheses often does not increase computational complexity compared to single-property cases.
conclusion: Combining multiple properties for abduction hypotheses is feasible without extra complexity, making such hypotheses more useful for applications.

title: CodeSentinel: A Three-Layer Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection In Code Contexts
authors: Po-Han Cheng, Chia-Mu Yu, Ying-Dar Lin, Yu-Sung Wu, Wei-Bin Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2606.19235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Code large language models increasingly retrieve external code context from repositories, documentation, issue threads, and coding-agent environments, creating an indirect prompt-injection surface where attackers hide instructions in comments, strings, identifiers, or decoy code. We propose CodeSentinel, a three-layer inference-time sanitizer. It uses Tree-sitter to extract high-risk model-facing CST nodes, then combines syntax-guided pre-filtering, CST-guided Dynamic Min-K\% scoring, and node perturbation analysis to detect adversarial and natural-looking semantic triggers. Detected nodes are removed or neutralized before reaching the downstream Code LLM. Across six recent attack families, \CodeSentinel achieves 0.80 average node-level F1, outperforming CodeGarrison, DePA, and KillBadCode.
tldr: CodeSentinel is a defense against indirect prompt injection in code large language models.
motivation: Code LLMs are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks where malicious instructions are hidden in external code context.
method: It uses Tree-sitter to extract CST nodes, then applies syntax-guided pre-filtering, CST-guided Dynamic Min-K% scoring, and node perturbation analysis to detect and neutralize adversarial nodes.
result: CodeSentinel achieves 0.80 average node-level F1 across six attack families, outperforming existing defenses.
conclusion: The three-layer sanitizer effectively mitigates indirect prompt injection in code contexts.

authors: Yifan Chen

motivation: Microplastic fibers are a major pollutant in the ocean, but their vertical distribution and residence time at the sea surface are poorly understood, which affects estimates of their environmental impact.
method: The authors combine field measurements of fiber length distributions at the sea surface and at 5 m depth with a theoretical model of fiber rise velocity and turbulent mixing.
result: They observe a surface enrichment of longer fibers relative to shorter ones, and their model explains this as a balance between buoyant rise and turbulent diffusion.
conclusion: The sea surface acts as a selective retention layer for longer microplastic fibers, which has implications for their transport, degradation, and ecological effects.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Dephasing Reduction In An Optically Guided Laser-plasma Accelerator
authors: Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, And Cédric Thaury
abstract:
Author(s): Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, and Cédric Thaury

Laser-plasma accelerators offer a compact means of producing high-energy electron beams, but their performance is fundamentally limited by dephasing between the accelerated electrons and the plasma wave. To overcome this limitation, we investigate the combination of plasma density tapering and optic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023274] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dephasing reduction in a laser-plasma accelerator using plasma density tapering and optical guiding.
motivation: Laser-plasma accelerators are limited by dephasing between electrons and the plasma wave; the authors aim to overcome this to improve electron beam energy and quality.
method: They combine plasma density tapering with optical guiding in an experiment to extend the acceleration length and reduce dephasing.
result: The technique successfully reduces dephasing, leading to higher-energy electron beams with improved properties.
conclusion: The approach offers a path to more compact and efficient laser-plasma accelerators for high-energy physics and other applications.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: To overcome the inherent bandwidth limitation of conventional resonance for applications requiring broadband response, such as flow stabilization.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance in a mechanical/acoustic system, showing how a resonant mode can maintain a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the typical bandwidth.
result: Super-resonance achieves a broadband out-of-phase response, enabling effective flow control over a wide frequency range.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and other areas requiring broadband operation.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]

abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, and Frédéric Merkt
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 029901] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on low-temperature ion-molecule reaction rates, with no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The original paper studied rotational and translational energy effects on ion-molecule reactions near 0 K; the erratum corrects errors in that work.
method: The erratum likely involves reanalysis of experimental data or correction of published results.
result: The erratum reports corrections to the original findings.
conclusion: The corrected results refine the understanding of low-temperature ion-molecule reaction dynamics.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Giomi

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: A continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces is formulated, resembling the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new path for materials design by linking mechanical deformation to quantum mechanical formalism.
conclusion: The work offers a novel approach to designing mechanical metamaterials, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is important for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and relate it to bulk hydrogel behavior through a force-response model.
result: They identify how protein unfolding and refolding cycles contribute to fatigue fracture and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a molecular-level understanding of fatigue in hydrogels and offers a design principle for improving their durability.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, and Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films induced by mesopore change, focusing on wood-derived films and vapor training processes.
motivation: To improve the plasticity and shaping of wood-derived films for practical applications.
method: A vapor training process is used to induce mesopore changes in nanocrystal films.
result: The process leads to improved plasticity and better shaping of the films.
conclusion: The vapor training method effectively enhances the mechanical properties of wood-derived nanocrystal films.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, and Ulrich S. Schwarz

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding mechanical forces at topological defects in curved epithelial tissues, which are relevant to developmental biology and disease.
method: A three-dimensional bubbly vertex model is developed to simulate curved epithelial sheets and analyze cell dynamics.
result: Cells at topological defects experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the role of geometry and mechanics in epithelial tissue remodeling.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, Van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, and Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding the hydrodynamics of microbial motility is important for biology and microfluidics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors used experimental three-dimensional flow measurements to study the flow field around a free-swimming microalga.
result: They discovered unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena that expand our understanding of microhydrodynamics.
conclusion: The findings have profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology, but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Active Hydrodynamic Theory Of Euchromatin And Heterochromatin
authors: S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, And Michael J. Shelley
abstract:
Author(s): S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, and Michael J. Shelley

Researchers develop a theoretical framework that shows how mechanical forces and flows drive the spatial segregation and nucleus-wide patterning of chromatin in cells.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021009] Published Thu Apr 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops an active hydrodynamic theory for the segregation of euchromatin and heterochromatin in cell nuclei.
motivation: To understand how mechanical forces and flows drive chromatin spatial organization and patterning in cells.
method: A theoretical framework based on active hydrodynamics, modeling chromatin as a two-fluid system with active stresses.
result: The model predicts spontaneous segregation and pattern formation consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: Mechanical forces and hydrodynamic flows are key drivers of chromatin compartmentalization in the nucleus.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A review of hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: To understand strong interaction (QCD) by studying charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights BESIII's leading role in high-precision measurements.
conclusion: Hadron spectroscopy in open-charm meson pairs provides crucial insights into QCD, with BESIII driving recent advances.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its contributions to various scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial compilation of colloquia, not a research study with a specific method.
result: No new research results; it is a retrospective overview.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory had a revolutionary impact on multiple areas of science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of planetary radar observations at Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To summarize the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system after its upgrade.
method: Review of radar techniques and key observations of planets, moons, and asteroids.
result: Highlights Arecibo's unique contributions to planetary science, including surface and subsurface characterization.
conclusion: Arecibo radar was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary exploration, and its loss leaves a gap.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Highlights Arecibo's major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo was a transformative instrument in radio astronomy, and its loss is significant for the field.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric and atmospheric physics.
motivation: To summarize the scientific contributions of the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research, highlighting its unique capabilities.
method: The paper reviews incoherent scatter radar theory and presents key results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, and optical instruments across multiple geospace science areas.
result: The review covers advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layer studies, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling, demonstrating the observatory's impact.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in advancing geospace science, and its legacy continues through ongoing data analysis and future research directions.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud processes.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising approach to resolving the precipitation bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare events that provide unique insights into stellar physics and neutron star formation; detecting gravitational waves alongside photons and neutrinos would enable multimessenger studies.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the current state of gravitational wave predictions from neutrino-driven core collapse supernovae and outlines strategies for multimessenger observation.
conclusion: The review highlights the potential of gravitational wave detection to probe the supernova central engine and the physics of neutron star formation, emphasizing the need for coordinated multimessenger campaigns.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a tension between the dipole in the cosmic microwave background and that in large-scale structure, challenging the cosmological principle.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by comparing the dipole anisotropy in galaxy/quasar catalogs with the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, including checks for biases and systematics.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model, but further work is needed to rule out systematic effects.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their observational signatures.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test self-interacting dark matter scenarios using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical models and observational data from galaxies to large-scale structures, including gravitational lensing and halo dynamics.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable hypothesis, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a review of viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The paper surveys current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and projects discovery potential across multiple search channels at the HL-LHC.
result: Stringent bounds have been placed on supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening focus on remaining viable models; projections indicate discovery potential for certain scenarios.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable but increasingly constrained; the HL-LHC offers the best near-term opportunity for discovery.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and diagnostics like neutrinos and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar properties and testing solar models.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma effects, and observational constraints from solar neutrinos and helioseismology.
result: It summarizes updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models that better match observations.
conclusion: The review consolidates recent progress in solar fusion physics, providing a benchmark for stellar astrophysics.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, focusing on fluid mechanics and two-phase flow.
motivation: Understanding bubble dynamics is important for natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The paper is a review summarizing advances in bubble dynamics, including turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and surfactants.
result: It highlights key findings and open questions in the field of two-phase flow.
conclusion: The review provides insights for modeling bubble behavior but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers deep-tissue optical contrast with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, where short laser pulses absorbed by tissue generate ultrasound waves detected externally.
result: The review discusses how optoacoustic microscopy impacts biological and clinical research and highlights multimodal combinations with optical techniques.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable noninvasive imaging tool, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can reveal physics from the first second after the Big Bang, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical predictions for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from cosmological sources and detection strategies.
result: Summarizes potential signals from phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe phenomena.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique probe of the early universe, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Atomic-scale 3d Insights Into Heteroepitaxial Mechanisms In Hcp/fcc, Bcc/fcc, And Fcc/fcc Core–shell Nanoparticles
authors: Xilong Mu, Yao Zhang, Kang’an Wang, Haoyi Tang, Zhiheng Xie, Zezhou Li, Xuemin Cao, Peng He And Jihan Zhou
abstract: Heteroepitaxy on nanocrystals of diverse crystal structures—hexagonal close-packed (hcp), body-centered cubic (bcc), and face-centered cubic (fcc)—is a powerful approach for engineering atomic arrangements. However, the mechanisms by which interfacial defects and strain relaxation accommodate structural mismatch remain poorly understood at the three-dimensional (3D) atomic scale. Here, we use atomic-resolution electron tomography to determine the 3D atomic structures and reveal heteroepitaxial mechanisms in Pt-based core–shell nanoparticles with diverse crystal structures including hcp/fcc Ru@Pt, bcc/fcc PdCu@Pt, and fcc/fcc Ru@Pt. We have identified distinct heteroepitaxial modes in these model systems, each mitigating the structural mismatch within a single particle: mixed coherent/semi-coherent growth in hcp/fcc Ru@Pt, coherent growth with strain sharing between core and shell in bcc/fcc PdCu@Pt, and oriented growth combined with twin proliferation in decahedral fcc/fcc Ru@Pt. The various semi-coherent growth modes in the hcp/fcc nanoparticle yield a 3D dislocation network at a scale below 10 nm, interconnected by Lomer–Cottrell, Hirth, and Shockley dislocations. The key heteroepitaxial mechanisms in these examined systems are quantitatively validated by interfacial energies derived from molecular statics simulations. We anticipate these insights will inform the targeted design of interfacial structures and enable precise strain engineering in core–shell nanomaterials.
tldr: This paper uses atomic-resolution electron tomography to study heteroepitaxial mechanisms in core-shell nanoparticles with different crystal structures.
motivation: Understanding how interfacial defects and strain relaxation accommodate structural mismatch in heteroepitaxial nanoparticles is crucial for engineering atomic arrangements.
method: Atomic-resolution electron tomography was used to determine 3D atomic structures of Pt-based core-shell nanoparticles (hcp/fcc Ru@Pt, bcc/fcc PdCu@Pt, fcc/fcc Ru@Pt), combined with molecular statics simulations to validate interfacial energies.
result: Distinct heteroepitaxial modes were identified: mixed coherent/semi-coherent growth in hcp/fcc, coherent growth with strain sharing in bcc/fcc, and oriented growth with twin proliferation in fcc/fcc. A 3D dislocation network below 10 nm was observed.
conclusion: The insights inform targeted design of interfacial structures and precise strain engineering in core-shell nanomaterials.
